| [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 | Promotion is audited in small persisted batches, ranked by expected yield, with decisions recorded apart from status changes | The owner's procedure of 2026-10-19 for finding entries whose evidence has outgrown their status. Candidates are triaged from metadata by a rubric that sets review order and never standing. They are reviewed five at a time, and each review ends in one of six dispositions with a specific blocker. Every step is persisted in record/promotion-audit/: a versioned queue.yaml with a hand-off block, one decision file per candidate, and one file per batch. | [ADR-064](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-064.md) | Copies of published articles on course, faculty and scholarly third-party pages count as lawful copies to read | The first pass over the Deferred LITs on 2026-10-29 read two works from copies on university course or group pages, and turned down similar copies of ten others as being "of unknown provenance". The owner ruled the refusals mistaken. | [ADR-076](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-076.md) v3 | Syntheses get a scheme of their own, SYNTHESIS, with statuses about the integration, a closed admission route, components whose standing is derived, and a generated current-account view | A synthesis filed as a CLAIM strains the CLAIM scheme four ways. Its components' voice and standing live in prose and drift. Its admission route has no field. CLAIM's status vocabulary has no word for "exhausted by its components", so the first synthesis that failed admission was marked Rejected, which says false. And nothing renders the record's current account, which the owner wants. This decision adds a SYNTHESIS scheme. It keeps three judgements apart: a status for the integrating account (Current, Proposed, Rejected, Superseded); an `admission` field (admitted or unadmitted), saying whether it earned an entry; and relations for its components. It has a closed `route`, required while admitted,: hypothesis, derived or integration. It has `integrates` and `premises` relations, whose targets' standing a generated view derives. The view, docs/current-account.md, is a Jinja template that sets out every Current or Proposed synthesis by line, with each component's status read from the component when the page is built. The five syntheses filed from "Individuation, Possibility, and Disposition" are moved into it as the demonstration, and their CLAIMs are Superseded by the new entries. ARG's `concludes` accepts a synthesis. Rejected: a route field on CLAIM; a CLAIM-only status vocabulary; DP's document rendering; the status quo. | Superseded — by [ADR-084](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-084.md) |
| [ADR-077](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-077.md) | A claim moved into the SYNTHESIS scheme keeps its standing and its relations: an admitted Active claim becomes a Current synthesis, and the scheme gains grounds, uses and corroborated_by so that nothing is dropped | The first synthesis review admitted [CLAIM-474](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-474.md) and could not move it. A review files every synthesis as Proposed, so an Active claim would have been demoted, and SYNTHESIS lacked grounds, uses and corroborated_by, so moving it would have dropped its readings, terms and corroboration. This decision amends [ADR-076](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-076.md) and the review's decision. A move keeps the claim's standing: an admitted Active CLAIM becomes a Current SYNTHESIS and a Proposed one stays Proposed, since the move changes the scheme that holds the entry, not the record's credence in it. The scheme gains the three fields, with their converses widened to match. A review still never sets a new synthesis Current. Its demonstration is [CLAIM-474](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-474.md)'s move. Rejected: moving as Proposed and asking for re-adoption; exempting adopted claims from the move; the owner setting each moved synthesis Current by hand. | Superseded — by [ADR-084](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-084.md) |
| [ADR-080](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-080.md) | A claim's rests_on may name a SYNTHESIS, so a claim whose premise moved into that scheme keeps its dependency; the argument chain walks the claim-to-claim steps through a pattern | Two synthesis reviews moved claims into the SYNTHESIS scheme that other live claims rested on: [CLAIM-544](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-544.md) on [CLAIM-545](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-545.md), and [CLAIM-338](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-338.md) on [CLAIM-336](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-336.md). A claim's `rests_on` accepted only CLAIMs, so those dependencies stayed on Superseded entries. This decision lets a claim's `rests_on` name a SYNTHESIS, with SYNTHESIS gaining the derived converse `supports`. The `argument` chain walked `rests_on`, and a luria chain stays within one scheme. So the chain now walks a named pattern, `rests_on_claim`, the claim-to-claim steps, in its place. Its demonstration repoints [CLAIM-338](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-338.md) and [CLAIM-544](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-544.md). Rejected: leaving the dependencies on Superseded claims; a separate field such as `presupposes` for a dependency on a synthesis; replacing the chain with a hand-written view. | Superseded — by [ADR-084](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-084.md) |
